⚠️⚠️ This circuit can be live even with the key removed. In the parking-light position (key turned left) the key comes out, yet this wire still has power. So before touching the wiring, always disconnect the battery's negative (−) terminal. Removing the key alone doesn't cut it.
⚠️ Don't replace a fuse with a higher-rated one. On the 500 all six fuses are 8 amps; each low beam has its own fuse, left and right, and each high beam shares one with side lights. Raise the rating and the wire it was meant to protect burns first. If a fuse keeps blowing, first find out why (something rubbing through and shorting to ground).
⚠️ Don't drive at night, in tunnels or in rain with headlights that don't work. Even one side out is a roadworthiness failure. Let bulbs cool before touching them — right after use you can't hold them bare-handed.

⭐ “All the headlights are out, but the side lights are on” — when you see this combination, the culprit is between the light switch and the column lever: the white wire itself, the switch contacts, or a connector come loose. It's all within reach behind the dash, the shortest stretch in this story.
If instead the side lights are out too, the culprit is further back — the light switch itself or the black wire from the ignition switch's 30/4 (the last row of the cross-check below is that scene). ⚠️ Then turning the key changes nothing. This is where people who've come this far get most confused: it isn't broken because the key does nothing. The key never did anything there in the first place.

But the column lever passes the power to neither side, so the front stays dark — push the column lever to II and they come on.
html.ダッシュのライトスイッチを入れても点かない。コラムレバーも下へ倒した。それでも前: You switch on the light switch on the dash. You push the column lever down. And the front still stays dark — that's the symptom on this page. Check with the key turned (a 500's headlights work with the key turned right and in the parking-light position, turned left; the reason is explained below).
html.ヒューズ箱に入る<b>手前の1本</b>（灰／赤）か、コラムレバーのロー側の接点: The single wire (grey/red) before the fuse box, or the low-side contact in the column lever
html.ヘッドライトの電源は、イグニッションスイッチの <code>30/4</code: The headlights' supply is the ignition switch's 30/4
html.ライトスイッチそのものか、その手前です。<b>ヘッドライトの問題ではありません<: The light switch itself, or before it. It isn't a headlight problem
html.ライトスイッチとコラムレバーを結ぶ<b>白い線</b>が切れたところ。ロー・ハイ: The white wire between the light switch and the column lever is broken. Low, high, left, right — all four go out. Yet the side lights stay on (the green wire branches off before this point).
html.ライトスイッチを入れ、コラムレバーを <b>II</b> まで倒す。白い線でコラ: Switch on the lights and push the column lever to II. The power that came along the white wire to the column lever passes to the low side, the single grey/red wire splits left and right in the fuse box, and both low beams light — with the key in position 1, or in position 2 turned left. After the repair, always check that both sides light on high beam, and that the indicator comes on. If you changed a bulb, the beam aim is worth checking too.

html.壁に向けて、<b>ローとハイを両方試してください</b>。消え方の組み合わせが6: Facing a wall, try both low and high. There are six combinations of what goes out, and each puts the culprit somewhere different. This is where this story is most useful.
html.左右のヘッドライトは<b>1つの電球の中にロー用とハイ用の2本のフィラメント</: Each headlight has two filaments, one for low and one for high, in a single bulb, with one shared ground for the return.
html.日が落ちてから気づくトラブルです。——この回路には、ここまでの7回に無かった特徴: A fault you notice after dark. — This circuit has something the seven parts so far didn't: low and high beams take different paths, and left and right are separate too. So just seeing what went out — right only, left only, low only, high only — almost pins down where the culprit is.
